name: Creality Falcon2 Pro 40W
tagline: 40W High-power diode with built-in air assist and color engraving gimmick
tldr: The 40W version of Creality's enclosed Falcon2 Pro, with a 1.6W infrared module for marking metal: a Class 1 cabinet that cuts thick plywood in fewer passes than the 22W. Worth the extra $450 if you cut more than you engrave.

priceRange.note: Official Creality store, Oct 2026: $1,349 to $1,999 depending on kit and 2W IR option

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: 15 mm basswood in one pass in Creality's 40W settings guide
Comes with a 1.6W module for fine-detail engraving
Fastest cuts and fills of the Falcon2 Pro tiers we list, in our benchmark
cons: $1,349 single unit on Creality's store (October 2026), well above the entry tier
Black acrylic beyond about 5 mm needs two passes
More smoke per job: plan an exhaust duct or purifier
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 40W SKU on Creality Falcon2 Pro. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Treat engraving and cutting as separate profiles. Push cut speeds only after test squares on your material. Compare CO₂ only when clear acrylic or all-day production enters the picture.
mainObjective: Maximum cut speed and depth in the line: engraving remains strong at tuned speeds

editorialDepth.advantages: Creality Falcon2 Pro 40W targets mixed engraving and wood-cutting weeks: fewer passes on basswood and dark acrylic than weaker SKUs in the same line.
editorialDepth.limitations: Wrong pick if you never engrave and only wanted the lowest price. Ultra-fine photo work can look better on an engraving-first SKU. Open-frame: safety and smoke are on you.

faq.question: How thick can the Falcon2 Pro 40W cut?
faq.answer: Creality's Falcon2 settings guide for the 40W module cuts 15 mm basswood in one pass at full power and 150 mm/min, and black acrylic at 4.6 mm in one pass or 7.6 mm in two. Our materials list stays at about 10 mm basswood for clean, repeatable cuts.

faq.question: Is the 40W worth $450 more than the 22W?
faq.answer: If you cut, yes: our benchmark took about 6–10 min for a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood against 9–14 min on the 22W, and the photo fill dropped from 17–26 to 12–18 min. The 40W listing also includes a 1.6W module for fine detail. Prices: $1,349 against $899 for the single unit on Creality's store, October 2026.

faq.question: Who should skip the 40W?
faq.answer: Buyers who mainly engrave photos and gifts: the 22W gives the same enclosure for less, and 40W cutting jobs produce more smoke for the extractor to handle.

standoutFeatures.title: 15 mm basswood in one pass
standoutFeatures.body: Creality's own settings for the 40W module cut 15 mm basswood in a single pass at 150 mm/min, deep enough for thick signs and sturdy boxes.

standoutFeatures.title: Second module for detail
standoutFeatures.body: The 40W listing includes a 1.6W module, so fine photo and line engraving does not suffer from the wide high-power beam.
